title: There's No Headcount Solution to AI-Powered Abuse: Introducing Cinder's AI Agent Platform
summary: Cinder Agents are AI systems trained on your content, your policies, and the validated decisions your own team makes over time.
body_text: For years, the standard playbook for platform safety was straightforward: hire reviewers, write policies, build queues, and repeat. If abuse spiked, you scaled the team. If a new harm type emerged, you added a workflow. Larger platforms layered in AI for detection at the edges, but the foundation was still human operations, and the model was still fundamentally linear. Then generative AI gave bad actors the ability to operate at machine scale, and the linear model collapsed. Bad actors can now generate harmful content at a scale and sophistication that simply wasn't possible a few years ago. The problem is growing exponentially, not linearly, and there's no headcount solution to an exponential problem. That's the challenge Cinder Agents were built for. What are Cinder Agents? Cinder Agents are AI systems trained on your content, your policies, and the validated decisions your own team makes over time. They're deployable against your most pressing problem from day one, and they get measurably sharper with every review cycle as your ground truth dataset grows. Every time a human reviewer makes a call, the agent learns from it. The result is an agent that enforces your standards at machine scale, with the context and judgment that comes from understanding your platform specifically. Each decision comes with a confidence score and human-readable reasoning, so your team isn't left seeing a decision that came out of a black box. The system runs as a continuous loop. Agents classify new content in real time with faster latency and auto-resolve the high-confidence cases. Anything in the gray area gets escalated to the right human reviewer with full context and a recommended action already attached. Your team stays in control, spending their time on the decisions that actually require judgment. Every review feeds back into the next retraining cycle, new agent versions are shadow-tested in production before deployment, and your agent next month is meaningfully sharper than your agent today. This is what it looks like when moderation quality becomes a metric you can actually move. An Agent for Every Problem One of the things we've learned working with companies like OpenAI, Character.AI, ElevenLabs, Midjourney, BeReal, and Depop is that platform safety problems don't come in one shape. What a marketplace worries about looks nothing like what a dating app or a foundation model lab is concerned with. So we didn't build a static agent. We built an architecture that lets you deploy dynamically updated agents for your specific problem, trained on your policies and tuned to the context of your platform. Content moderation. Whether your team thinks in terms of a hate speech agent, a CSAM agent, or a harassment agent, Cinder's content moderation architecture covers the full spectrum and trains each enforcement layer on your specific policies, not a generic taxonomy that treats every platform the same. It handles text, image, audio, video, and live stream in one system, with sub-500ms latency so harmful content is stopped before it reaches your users. It covers hate speech, CSAM, NCII, extremism, harassment, scams, and AI-generated harm, and it writes what it learns from your team's reviews back into the system that runs your operation. Learn more about the content moderation agent . Case investigation. Coordinated abuse rarely shows up as a single clean violation. It moves across accounts, content, reports, devices, payments, and time, and a queue item can show you the latest flag without revealing the pattern behind it. The case investigation agent pulls accounts, content, behaviors, prior decisions, and related entities into one structured view, surfaces the pattern, and resolves the cases it can with confidence. The ones that need human judgment go to the right reviewer with full context and a recommended action already attached. Every resolved case becomes part of the intelligence layer that helps the next one move faster. Learn more about case investigation . Counterfeit and IP protection. Counterfeits erode trust and drive down what legitimate sellers can charge. DMCA notices pile up faster than most legal teams can answer. Brand impersonation siphons customers into scams that look exactly like you, and the trust cost compounds in ways you can't fully refund. The IP and copyright agent is trained on your platform's specific fraud signatures and pulls external context from rights-holder databases, marketplace cross-listings, reverse image lookups, and web signals to make calls that a static classifier never could. Every action is documented and defensible, before a claim becomes a chargeback or a customer who never comes back. Learn more about IP and copyright protection . User fraud and ATO. Fake accounts, synthetic identities, account takeovers, and bot rings don't announce themselves cleanly. They show up as patterns across accounts, devices, events, relationships, and history. The fraud agent connects those signals and evaluates them against your policies and your platform's specific fraud signatures rather than generic models that bad actors already know how to evade. Suspicious behavior is detected before it spreads, with the surrounding evidence and reasoning your team needs to act quickly. Learn more about fraud and ATO detection . Custom agents. Custom agents run on the same architecture as everything else in Cinder. Same policy configuration, same observability, same closed-loop retraining, same human escalation paths. The difference is that you define the problem. Whether that's avatar misuse, romance scams, election interference, or something no vendor has a name for yet, you wire your policies and your data into an agent built for the exact risk your platform faces, and run it on the same platform already powering your operation. You can build one independently or work with our services team to design and train it alongside your operators. Learn more about custom agents . What AI Agents Look Like in Practice Across our customer base, Cinder protects more than 3 billion users, automates 94% of human review, and processes over 400 million events daily. Teams come to Cinder needing agents that can scale with their product without losing the judgment their policies require. We've been able to deliver that by training every agent on the decisions a platform's own team has already made, so enforcement stays aligned with their standards as volume grows, and gets sharper with every review cycle rather than drifting from it. For example, Character.AI needed a way to enforce policy on AI-generated personas at scale, including detecting whether characters were modeled on real people, living or deceased, and routing those cases appropriately. With Cinder, they reduced their human moderation queue by more than 50% while maintaining the quality bar their team had set. Their reviewers didn't disappear. They moved up the stack, focusing on the cases that genuinely require human judgment rather than spending their time on decisions an agent could make with high confidence. Black Forest Labs came to us before launching FLUX and needed adversarial testing rigorous enough to match their release velocity. Cinder Agents stress-tested the model against real-world attack patterns, surfaced edge cases before they became public incidents, and helped them launch 10x safer than benchmark industry models, with a greater than 90% reduction in CSAM and NCII vulnerability. Zello, a push-to-talk platform used by first responders and field teams, needed to catch repeat offenders faster across a high-volume, real-time environment. With Cinder, they now take down 3x more repeat-offender accounts, and 50% of all bans are executed automatically through orchestrated agent workflows without human intervention on each individual decision. One entertainment streaming customer launched a major new messaging feature and had the full safety infrastructure in place within two weeks, a deployment that would historically have taken months of internal engineering work. That speed matters when you're introducing a new surface that bad actors will probe from day one. Agents That Scale Your Team Cinder Agents handle the decisions that don't need a human, so that the decisions that do get the attention they deserve. Every agent is built with human review in the loop by design, not as a fallback. Your team sets the policies, reviews the edge cases, and every call they make sharpens the agent for the next one. The agents get the volume. Your reviewers get the cases that actually matter. The trust and safety teams we've worked with closest don't talk about this as automation. They talk about it as finally having enough leverage to do the job well. If you're dealing with abuse at scale and wondering whether your current approach can keep up, we'd like to show you what Cinder Agents can do for your platform. Explore Cinder Agents .

title: Embedded: Last-Level Caches Matter Even More in the HBM Era
summary: A decade ago, a high-end server processor might have accessed 50 to 100 GB/s of memory bandwidth. At the time, that seemed impressive. Today, AI
body_text: Home » Newsroom » Blog » Embedded: Last-Level Caches Matter Even More in the HBM Era Embedded: Last-Level Caches Matter Even More in the HBM Era Aug 6, 2026 André Bonnardot < 1 min read A decade ago, a high-end server processor might have accessed 50 to 100 GB/s of memory bandwidth. At the time, that seemed impressive. Today, AI accelerators routinely consume 3 to 8 TB/s of memory bandwidth, roughly 30 to 100 times that of their predecessors. This dramatic increase in demand has driven the rapid adoption of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and other data-intensive applications. By placing multiple stacks of DRAM dies in the same package as the main system-on-chip (SoC) die, HBM provides memory bandwidth levels that would be difficult—or impossible—to achieve with traditional DDR memory alone. Many people assume that once HBM enters the picture, memory bottlenecks become a thing of the past. Unfortunately, the reality is more complicated. HBM offers a much bigger pipe, but more bandwidth does not automatically translate into a faster or more efficient system. As a result, last-level caches (LLCs) are more important today than ever before Modern SoCs are data-movement machines Today’s SoCs are astonishingly complex devices containing hundreds of intellectual property (IP) blocks, including CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, DSPs, hardware accelerators, DMA engines, security functions, and more. These blocks communicate via one or more networks-on-chip (NoCs), with some advanced SoCs employing dozens of NoCs, each optimized for different traffic types and performance requirements. title: Best time to visit Rwanda: Weather, seasons and money tips
summary: The best time to visit Rwanda is the long dry season from June to September, ideal for gorilla trekking. See the weather by month and money tips. Read on.
body_text: Rwanda is one of Africa's most rewarding travel destinations, known for its breathtaking mountain gorillas, rolling green hills and well-maintained national parks. If you're planning a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife adventure or simply want to explore Kigali and the country's natural beauty, when you visit can have a big impact on your experience. The country's weather changes throughout the year, affecting everything from hiking conditions and safari experiences to accommodation prices and visitor numbers. Picking the right season can mean clearer forest trails, better wildlife sightings and a more comfortable trip overall. For most travellers, the long dry season from June to September is the best time to visit Rwanda, especially for gorilla trekking. The short dry season between December and February is another excellent option. In this guide, you'll discover the best months to visit, what each season offers and practical tips to help you make the most of your budget. Understanding Rwanda's weather and seasons Rwanda enjoys a mild highland climate throughout the year, so temperatures remain comfortable regardless of when you visit. Instead of dramatic changes between summer and winter, the country experiences two dry seasons and two rainy seasons, with each offering a different travel experience. The weather is influenced more by rainfall than temperature, making the timing of your trip especially important for outdoor activities. The long dry season runs from June to September and is widely regarded as the best time for gorilla trekking, hiking and wildlife viewing. The short dry season, from December to February, also brings pleasant conditions with fewer muddy trails. The long rainy season falls between March and May, while the short rainy season lasts from October to November. Rain usually comes in heavy showers rather than lasting all day, but trails can become slippery and some outdoor activities more challenging during these months. Also read: Best countries to work in East Africa When is the best time for gorilla trekking in Rwanda? If seeing Rwanda's famous mountain gorillas is at the top of your travel list, June to September is generally the best time to visit. This is the country's long dry season, when forest trails in Volcanoes National Park are firmer, less muddy and easier to navigate. While gorilla sightings are possible throughout the year, drier conditions make the trekking experience more comfortable, especially on steep mountain paths. The popularity of this season also means demand is at its highest. Gorilla trekking permits are limited and often sell out months in advance, particularly during peak holiday periods. If you're planning to travel between June and September, book your permit as early as possible, along with your accommodation and transport. Planning ahead not only secures your preferred dates but also gives you a wider choice of lodges near the national park. Where to go in Rwanda and the best time to visit The ideal time to visit Rwanda depends on what you want to experience. While the dry seasons are generally the most comfortable for travelling, each destination has its own highlights that make certain months especially rewarding. Lake Kivu If your idea of a holiday is slowing down and enjoying beautiful scenery, Lake Kivu is at its best between June and September. Sunny days and calm waters make it perfect for boat cruises, kayaking, lakeside cafés and beach resorts. The pleasant weather also makes exploring nearby towns much more enjoyable. Nyungwe National Park Nature lovers will appreciate Nyungwe National Park during the June to September and December to February dry seasons. With less rain, forest trails are easier to hike, making chimpanzee trekking, canopy walks and waterfall trails more accessible. Wildlife viewing is also more comfortable when paths are firm and visibility is better. Kigali Kigali is a destination you can enjoy throughout the year thanks to its mild climate and well-planned streets. Even so, the dry months are ideal for walking through neighbourhoods, visiting museums, shopping at local markets and enjoying the city's cafés without having to plan around frequent afternoon showers. Also read: Best places remote workers travel to in early 2026 When is the cheapest time to visit Rwanda If your priority is saving money, March to May is usually the cheapest time to visit Rwanda. This is the long rainy season, when fewer tourists travel. As demand falls, many hotels, luxury lodges and tour operators offer lower prices, making it easier to enjoy Rwanda on a smaller budget. The trade-off is that you'll encounter more rain, especially in the afternoons, and some hiking trails can become muddy. However, you'll also enjoy quieter national parks, fewer crowds and lush green landscapes that many photographers consider the country's most beautiful. One important cost never changes: gorilla trekking permits. Rwanda keeps permit prices fixed at $1,500 per person throughout the year, so travelling in the rainy season won't reduce this expense. Your savings will come from accommodation, flights and selected tour packages rather than the trekking permit itself. Managing money while travelling in Rwanda The official currency in Rwanda is the Rwandan franc (RWF), but you won't always pay in cash. Many hotels, restaurants, supermarkets and tour operators accept card payments, and you'll likely need a card for online bookings before your trip as well. If you're making payments online or in person, especially where Visa is accepted, the Grey virtual card is a convenient way to pay for shopping, accommodation, transport and other travel expenses. Grey is also useful beyond card payments. If you need to pay a tour operator, send money to your family or transfer funds while you're travelling, you can send USD, GBP or EUR directly from your Grey account. Simply download the Grey app or open an account to manage your foreign currencies, international transfers and travel spending from one place. Frequently asked questions When is the best time for gorilla trekking? The best time for gorilla trekking is during Rwanda's dry seasons, from June to September and December to February. Forest trails are firmer, hiking is easier and photography conditions are better. Because permits are limited, book your trekking permit and accommodation several months before your planned travel dates. How much is a gorilla permit? A gorilla trekking permit costs $1,500 per person for international visitors. This price remains the same throughout the year, regardless of the season. While hotels and flights may become cheaper during the rainy months, the permit itself is never discounted, so include it in your travel budget early. What is the rainy season? Rwanda has two rainy seasons. The longest runs from March to May, bringing heavier rainfall, while a shorter rainy period occurs between October and November. Although rain can make hiking trails muddier, landscapes become greener, parks are quieter and accommodation prices are often lower during these months. Is Rwanda expensive? Rwanda is known for premium eco-tourism, particularly gorilla trekking and luxury lodges. However, independent travellers can still enjoy affordable guesthouses, local restaurants and public transport. Your total cost depends on your travel style, making Rwanda suitable for both luxury holidays and carefully planned budget-friendly trips alike. What currency does Rwanda use? Rwanda's official currency is the Rwandan franc (RWF). Many safari lodges, hotels and tour operators also accept US dollars, especially for larger payments. Carrying some local cash is useful for markets, taxis and smaller businesses, while cards are increasingly accepted in major towns and cities. Can I pay by card in Rwanda? Yes. Many hotels, restaurants and larger businesses accept Visa and Mastercard, particularly in Kigali and tourist areas. For online bookings and payments where Visa is accepted, the Grey Visa card is an ideal option.

title: The Alt Protein Project welcomes 15 new student groups
summary: Fifteen groups from universities around the world join GFI’s student community, the Alt Protein Project
body_text: Meet the 2026 APP cohort Africa The Ahmadu Bello University Alt Protein Project Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, located in northern Nigeria, is already home to institutes primed for alternative protein research, such as the Institute for Agricultural Research and the Biotechnology Center, which specializes in plant tissue culture and molecular genetics. The ABU APP founders join our community with backgrounds in student organizing via their work with Effective Altruism and Planted’s Eat For Impact campaign. Additionally, ABU is located near Kano and Kaduna, Nigerian hot spots for agro-processing and manufacturing, respectively. Drawing on these regional strengths and an entrepreneurial student community, the ABU APP is well positioned to advance alternative proteins across northern Nigeria. The MAU Yola Alt Protein Project Located in Northeastern Nigeria, Modibbo Adama University, Yola (MAU Yola) is a federal technology university devoted to advancing scientific research through alternative protein-adjacent programs in food science, plant science, and biotechnology. The university’s existing research on regional crops such as cowpea and bambaranuts provides fertile ground for alternative protein research. Driven by a commitment to sustainability and with strong backgrounds in food science, the MAU Yola APP aims to cultivate the next generation of alternative protein champions. Europe The Helsinki Alt Protein Project The University of Helsinki is Finland’s oldest and largest university. The university has prolific food sensory and material science programs, alongside their Viikki food design factory: a center devoted to sustainable solutions for food system transformation. While much government investment and alternative protein research has already come out of Finland, the Helsinki APP seeks to catalyze more interdisciplinary collaboration on their campus and expand educational opportunities for students entering the field. The Manchester Alt Protein Project The University of Manchester is one of the UK’s largest institutions and consistently ranks among the world’s leading universities for sustainability. The Manchester APP will join a campus of existing innovative food research initiatives, such as their Biocatalysis and Protein Engineering Centre for Sustainable Synthesis and the Sustainable Consumption Institute. The Manchester APP is also set up for key industry connections through ADM’s new food innovation center on campus and university spin-outs like Cytotrait and Bright Biotech. India The GBU Smart Protein Project Gujarat Biotechnology University (GBU) was established to accelerate biotechnology research and prepare the next generation of scientific innovators. Through partnerships with the University of Edinburgh, the Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM), and the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC), GBU is deeply connected to India’s biotechnology ecosystem. The GBU Smart Protein Project will leverage these relationships to strengthen collaboration, investment, and policy development for alternative proteins across Gujarat and beyond. The Sathyabama Smart Protein Project The Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology, located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India, is already home to alternative protein research across all three pillars (plant-based, cultivated, and fermentation-derived proteins). For example, researchers within the university’s National Facility for Coastal and Marine Research are studying protein engineering applications and bioprinting for cultivated meat applications. With strong programs in biotechnology, food science, and environmental science, the Sathyabama SPP is eager to build an alternative protein ecosystem that is even stronger and more connected. Latin America The UADE Alt Protein Project The Argentine University of Enterprise (Universidad Argentina de la Empresa) is located in Buenos Aires, Argentina– a hub for Argentinian food technology. UADE hosts strong programs in food science, chemistry, and biotechnology, as well as UADE Labs, a university initiative devoted to driving scientific innovation in fields like agriculture and biosciences. The university’s food engineering program, the only South American program to be certified by the Institute of Food Technologists, will also provide a solid foundation for the UADE APP to build alternative protein education and research on campus. The UNAHUR Alt Protein Project The National University of Hurlingham (UNAHUR) joins the Alt Protein Project’s growing cohort in the Buenos Aires province of Argentina. The UNAHUR APP is excited to capitalize on their university’s existing sustainable and food technology-focused infrastructure, including the Pilot Food Plant, the Biofactory, and the Research Laboratory for New Foods and Nutrition. With ongoing research in plant-based dairy alternatives and protein development already underway, the UNAHUR APP aims to connect more students with hands-on research while inspiring new projects. The UNLP Alt Protein Project The National University of La Plata (UNLP), also located in Buenos Aires, Argentina, is home to three research institutes that will support alternative protein research and development: the Institute of Biotechnology and Microbiology, the Research and Development Center for Industrial Fermentations, and the Center for Research and Development in Food Science and Technology. The UNLP APP team is eager to use their university’s expertise in fermentation and protein characterization to expand student-led research and collaboration. North America The Dartmouth Alt Protein Project Dartmouth College is a private, Ivy League university located in New Hampshire, US. With its long history of liberal arts education, Dartmouth brings unique strengths to the APP global community. The founding APP team has already attended APP-supported events like the Food4Thought festival and brings relevant leadership experience from mission-aligned student groups like Effective Altruism, Better Food Foundation, and Allied Scholars for Animal Protection. Students can pursue alternative protein innovation through the Magnuson Center for Entrepreneurship and engage with agricultural policy through the school’s many partnerships with leading policy institutions and think tanks. Dartmouth’s Thayer School of Engineering further strengthens the campus with cutting-edge research in biotechnology and materials science, creating new opportunities for alternative protein innovation. The McGill Alt Protein Project McGill University, located in Quebec, Canada, is a leading hub for research in alternative protein-related fields, including bioresource engineering, food science, and human nutrition. The founding members of the McGill APP bring extensive expertise in sustainable food systems, with research spanning life cycle assessment, circular bioeconomies, and public policy. Their collaborations with organizations including the National Research Council Canada and Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, their creation of the CellAg Sustainability and AI Collective, and their funding from the New Harvest Student Activation Fund prove that the team is well set to build a strong alternative protein community. The UMBC Alt Protein Project The University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) is home to bwtech , a research and technology park including a startup accelerator, scale-up program, and entrepreneur-in-residence program. The school has strong STEM programs through their colleges of Natural and Mathematical Sciences, and Engineering and Information Technology. The UMBC APP team is excited to bring alternative proteins to a campus that is already passionate about the environment, sustainability, and innovation. The University of Alberta Alt Protein Project The University of Alberta’s food science program and active cellular agriculture research community provide an excellent academic foundation for students interested in alternative proteins. Researchers are advancing topics ranging from faba bean applications for plant-based meat to beef cell line development through the university’s Institute for Cellular Agriculture. The Alberta APP founders are a part of New Harvest’s “Defining, Enhancing, and Refining Agricultural Inputs and the Supply Chains of Cellular Agriculture and Biomanufacturing of Food” fellowship, bringing substantial research experience. The founding team has also already begun building an alternative protein community on campus through tastings, laboratory tours, and educational workshops. The University of Guelph Alt Protein Project Situated in Canada’s leading agrifood and food technology hub, the University of Guelph benefits from proximity to thousands of food companies and key government agencies such as the Ontario Ministry of Agriculture. The university’s engineering school also hosts the Canadian Food Engineering Conference, reflecting its leadership in food innovation. Faculty are advancing alternative protein research through projects such as Dr. Guneet Kaur’s work in microbial engineering and waste valorization and Dr. Ashutosh Singh’s research on processing methods to improve plant-based protein digestibility. Furthermore, the university’s food science program provides expertise in product development, sensory science, and agricultural innovation. The University of Nebraska Alt Protein Project The University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) is a land-grant university known for its rigorous programs in agriculture and natural resources. Centers such as the Plant Science Innovation Center and the Nebraska Food for Health Center provide valuable infrastructure for alternative protein research. The university is already home to many alternative protein research projects, such as Dr. Kaustav Majumder’s research on plant protein functionality and bioactive peptides for human health and collaborations with Dr. Toshihiro Obata and Dr. Jinliang Yang to study crops such as soybean, maize, and wheat. The UNL APP seeks to connect students with these research opportunities while fostering an alternative protein community across campus. To learn more about the 80+ groups of the Alt Protein Project or to connect with a group near you, visit our group directory or reach out to us directly.

title: AAP 2023 Pediatric Obesity Guidelines: A Parent's Plain-Language Summary
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics' 2023 Clinical Practice Guideline is the first comprehensive U.S. guideline for evaluating and treating childhood obesity. This plain-language summary explains what it actually recommends by age and BMI: annual BMI screening from age 2, intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment (IHBLT) as the foundation, weight-loss pharmacotherapy offered for consideration at 12 and older, and a surgery-evaluation referral at 13 and older with severe obesity, with equity, weight stigma, and mental-health screening named as foundational. Links to the primary source throughout.
body_text: The AAP 2023 obesity guidelines are the American Academy of Pediatrics' first comprehensive Clinical Practice Guideline for the evaluation and treatment of children and teens with obesity, published in January 2023. The guideline recommends regular BMI screening from age 2, intensive lifestyle treatment as the foundation, weight-loss medication offered for consideration for adolescents 12 and older who meet criteria, and a surgery-evaluation referral for adolescents 13 and older with severe obesity. This page explains each part in plain language and links to the source. Key Takeaways The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) 2023 Clinical Practice Guideline is the first comprehensive U.S. pediatric obesity guideline and treats childhood obesity as a chronic condition. The foundation is intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment (IHBLT). The most effective programs deliver 26 or more hours of face-to-face, family-based contact over 3 to 12 months. The guideline recommends offering weight-loss pharmacotherapy to adolescents 12 and older with obesity (BMI at or above the 95th percentile), as an adjunct to lifestyle treatment, according to each medication's indications, risks, and benefits. For adolescents 13 and older with severe obesity (BMI at or above 120 percent of the 95th percentile for age and sex), the guideline recommends offering a referral to a comprehensive metabolic and bariatric surgery center for evaluation. The recommendation is for a referral to be evaluated, not for surgery itself. The guideline names equity, weight stigma, and mental-health screening (including disordered-eating screening) as foundational. The 2023 guideline replaces the 2007 stepped-care, watchful-waiting model and recommends evaluating earlier. This page summarizes and links to the guideline. It is not the official guideline. What the AAP 2023 guideline actually says Age BMI threshold AAP recommendation Balance implementation Age 2+ All BMI percentiles Annual BMI screening (KAS 1) Built into visit intake Age 6+ BMI ≥ 95th percentile Intensive lifestyle treatment (IHBLT), 26+ contact-hours (KAS 11) Unlimited-coaching IHBLT base layer Age 12+ BMI ≥ 95th percentile Offer weight-loss pharmacotherapy as an adjunct (KAS 12) DABOM-led shared-decision conversation Age 13+ BMI ≥ 120% of 95th percentile (severe obesity) Offer surgery-evaluation referral (KAS 13) Referral to in-person comprehensive centers The Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG) was published on January 9, 2023, in Pediatrics ( Hampl SE et al., doi:10.1542/peds.2022-060640 ). It is the AAP's first comprehensive treatment guideline for pediatric obesity, building on evidence accumulated since the 2007 AAP Expert Committee report ( Barlow SE et al., Pediatrics 2007 ). Four themes organize the recommendations: (1) treat childhood obesity as a chronic condition that benefits from sustained care; (2) treat the whole child, not just the BMI number, including behavioral health, family-system care, and social factors; (3) intervene early once treatment is offered, rather than watchful waiting; (4) eliminate weight stigma from care delivery. How the AAP defines overweight, obesity, and severe obesity Direct answer: The CPG defines overweight as BMI in the 85th to under 95th percentile, obesity as BMI at or above the 95th percentile, and severe obesity as BMI at or above 120 percent of the 95th percentile for age and sex. BMI percentile compares a child's BMI to a reference population of children the same age and sex on the CDC growth charts. A BMI at the 95th percentile means the child's BMI is higher than 95 percent of children the same age and sex. Verbatim from KAS 1: "Pediatricians and other PHCPs should measure height and weight, calculate BMI, and assess BMI percentile using age- and sex-specific CDC growth charts or growth charts for children with severe obesity at least annually for all children 2 to 18 years of age to screen for overweight (BMI ≥85th percentile to <95th percentile), obesity (BMI ≥95th percentile), and severe obesity (BMI ≥120% of the 95th percentile for age and sex)." Severe obesity has two classes. Class 2 is a BMI of 120 to under 140 percent of the 95th percentile, or 35 to under 39 kg/m², whichever is lower for age and sex. Class 3 is a BMI at or above 140 percent of the 95th percentile, or at or above 40 kg/m², whichever is lower. Severe obesity is defined by BMI alone; the CPG does not require any specific comorbidity. IHBLT: intensive lifestyle treatment is the foundation Direct answer: The CPG recommends IHBLT as first-line treatment for children 6 and older with overweight or obesity, with 26 or more hours of contact over 3 to 12 months for the most effective effect. IHBLT stands for Intensive Health Behavior and Lifestyle Treatment: structured, family-centered programs that combine nutrition counseling, physical-activity support, behavioral skills, and parent engagement. The CPG recommends 26 or more hours of contact time over 3 to 12 months, the threshold the evidence base associates with meaningfully better and more durable BMI reduction. KAS 11, verbatim: "Pediatricians and other PHCPs should provide or refer children 6 years and older (Grade B) and may provide or refer children 2 through 5 years of age (Grade C) with overweight (BMI ≥85th percentile to <95th percentile) and obesity (BMI ≥95th percentile) to intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. Health behavior and lifestyle treatment is more effective with greater contact hours; the most effective treatment includes 26 or more hours of face-to-face, family-based, multicomponent treatment over a 3- to 12-month period." The 26-hour figure comes from a systematic review the CPG cites ( O'Connor EA et al., JAMA 2017 ). Programs reaching 26 or more hours produced meaningful BMI reduction with maintenance; shorter programs did not. The 2024 USPSTF statement ( Nicholson WK et al., JAMA 2024 ) confirmed the same standard. IHBLT is the base layer under every other recommendation. Pharmacotherapy and surgery, where they apply, are offered as adjuncts to IHBLT, not as replacements. When the AAP recommends considering medication Direct answer: The CPG recommends offering weight-loss pharmacotherapy to adolescents 12 and older with obesity (BMI at or above the 95th percentile), as an adjunct to lifestyle treatment, with attention to each medication's indications, risks, and benefits, and with shared decision-making. KAS 12, verbatim: "Pediatricians and other PHCPs should offer adolescents 12 years and older with obesity (BMI ≥95th percentile) weight loss pharmacotherapy, according to medication indications, risks, and benefits, as an adjunct to health behavior and lifestyle treatment." Two clarifications often get lost. First, the recommendation is to offer the consideration, not to prescribe automatically. Second, the eligibility threshold is age and BMI, not a specific comorbidity. KAS 12 applies to adolescents 12 and older with obesity. The CPG directs clinicians to evaluate and treat obesity-related conditions (type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, dyslipidemia, fatty liver, sleep apnea, and others) alongside pharmacotherapy, not as a precondition for it. The evidence base includes the STEP TEENS trial of once-weekly semaglutide ( Weghuber D et al., NEJM 2022 ). In that trial, 201 adolescents ages 12 to under 18 with obesity were treated for 68 weeks; adolescents who received once-weekly semaglutide alongside behavioral lifestyle support reduced their BMI by an average of 16.1 percent, while those who received placebo with the same lifestyle support increased BMI by 0.6 percent. Other medications referenced in the CPG include metformin, phentermine-topiramate, liraglutide, and orlistat. Each has its own FDA-approved age, indication, risks, and benefits. When the AAP recommends a surgery-evaluation referral Direct answer: For adolescents 13 and older with severe obesity, the CPG recommends offering a referral to a comprehensive pediatric metabolic and bariatric surgery center for evaluation. The recommendation is for a referral to be evaluated, not for surgery itself. KAS 13, verbatim (excerpt): "...adolescents 13 years and older with severe obesity (BMI ≥120% of the 95th percentile for age and sex) for evaluation for metabolic and bariatric surgery..." The recommendation is precise: it is a referral to a comprehensive center, not a recommendation to operate. A multidisciplinary team evaluates whether surgery is the right next step over months, considering medical, nutritional, behavioral-health, and family components. Severe obesity here is defined by BMI alone (Class 2 or Class 3), not by comorbidity. The evidence base includes the Teen-LABS cohort ( Inge TH et al., NEJM 2016 and 2019 ). At 3 years post-surgery, weight reduction averaged about 27 percent and remission rates were high for type 2 diabetes (95 percent), prediabetes (76 percent), and elevated blood pressure (74 percent). At 5 years, adolescents undergoing gastric bypass had better remission rates than adults for type 2 diabetes (86 vs 53 percent) and high blood pressure (68 vs 41 percent). Teen-LABS also documented higher rates of micronutrient deficiencies in adolescents. The 5-year remission figures cited above come specifically from Roux-en-Y gastric bypass ( Inge et al., NEJM 2019 ). The two current standard adolescent procedures are laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and vertical sleeve gastrectomy; both have strong long-term Teen-LABS durability data. Surgery is a serious decision, and the CPG recommendation reflects that: a referral to a center that can support the family through evaluation. What the AAP names as foundational: equity, stigma, and mental-health screening Direct answer: The CPG names equity, weight stigma, and mental-health screening (including disordered-eating screening) as foundational to obesity care, not as optional add-ons. The guideline is built on a family-centered, non-stigmatizing approach. KAS 9, verbatim: "Pediatricians and other PHCPs should treat overweight (BMI ≥85th percentile to <95th percentile) and obesity (BMI ≥95th percentile) in children and adolescents, following the principles of the medical home and the chronic care model, using a family-centered and nonstigmatizing approach that acknowledges obesity's biologic, social, and structural drivers." The CPG names mental-health screening, including for depression, anxiety, and disordered eating, as part of routine obesity evaluation. It addresses the concern that intensive treatment could increase eating-disorder risk by recommending screening and care, not deferred treatment. The CPG also instructs clinicians to use person-first language and engage families as partners. Common parent concerns about the 2023 rollout (over-medicalization, age thresholds, surgery in adolescents, stigma, eating-disorder risk) are not unaddressed in the guideline. They are named explicitly, and the recommendations sit on top of that foundation. How the 2023 guideline differs from the 2007 recommendations Direct answer: The 2023 CPG replaces the 2007 expert committee recommendations, which used a stepped-care, watchful-waiting model. The 2023 guideline recommends evaluating and intervening earlier. The 2007 framework ( Barlow SE; Expert Committee; Pediatrics 2007 ) used a Stage 1 to Stage 4 stepped-care model that progressed only after a defined trial at each prior stage. The 2023 CPG moves away from watchful waiting and recommends evaluation and treatment offers as soon as a child meets criteria, with intensity tailored to BMI category, age, and clinical picture. The CPG has not been substantively revised; a January 2024 Statement of Correction (Pediatrics 2024;153(1):e2023064612) updated one bibliographic reference only, leaving every Key Action Statement intact. How Blueberry Balance implements the AAP framework Direct answer: Blueberry Balance is one operational implementation of the AAP framework, built around the IHBLT base layer with DABOM-led specialist evaluation, and stepped-care pharmacotherapy consideration when indicated. Balance refers to comprehensive in-person centers for surgery evaluation. The Balance protocol maps onto the AAP recommendations. The unlimited-coaching IHBLT base layer is designed to meet or exceed the 26-hour intensity bar from KAS 11. A DABOM-credentialed pediatrician leads the medical evaluation and, when indicated, the pharmacotherapy conversation under KAS 12. Balance does not perform surgery; when a KAS 13 surgery-evaluation referral is clinically appropriate, Balance's role is to support it. Balance is a pediatric obesity medicine specialty layer that works alongside the child's existing pediatrician. Frequently asked questions Does the AAP recommend Wegovy for 12-year-olds? The 2023 guideline recommends offering weight-loss pharmacotherapy consideration to adolescents 12 and older with obesity (BMI at or above the 95th percentile), as an adjunct to lifestyle treatment, according to each medication's indications, risks, and benefits. The CPG does not name a single medication by brand. Wegovy (semaglutide) is one option in this class, supported by the STEP TEENS trial (Weghuber 2022); whether it is right for a particular adolescent depends on clinical evaluation and shared decision-making. Does the AAP recommend weight-loss surgery for 13-year-olds? The 2023 guideline recommends a referral for evaluation, not surgery itself. For adolescents 13 and older with severe obesity (BMI at or above 120 percent of the 95th percentile for age and sex), the CPG recommends offering a referral to a comprehensive pediatric metabolic and bariatric surgery center, where a multidisciplinary team determines whether surgery is the right next step. Most referred adolescents do not proceed straight to surgery; the evaluation itself runs for months. Did the AAP retract or revise the 2023 guideline? No. The CPG has not been retracted or substantively revised. A single Statement of Correction was published in January 2024 that updated one bibliographic reference (#505) only. No recommendation language was changed and no Key Action Statement was modified. How does the AAP guideline address eating-disorder risk? The CPG names disordered-eating screening as part of routine obesity evaluation. The guideline addresses the concern that intensive treatment could increase eating-disorder risk by recommending screening for and addressing those risks within care, not deferring treatment. It also instructs clinicians to use person-first language and a family-centered, non-stigmatizing approach. Is Blueberry Balance an AAP-recommended program? The AAP does not endorse specific programs. Balance is one operational implementation of the AAP framework. The Balance protocol is built around the IHBLT base layer described in KAS 11, with DABOM-led specialist evaluation and stepped-care pharmacotherapy consideration where it is clinically appropriate. Does the AAP still recommend watchful waiting? No. The 2023 guideline replaces the 2007 stepped-care, watchful-waiting model. KAS 11 recommends that clinicians provide or refer to intensive lifestyle treatment for children 6 and older with obesity once they meet criteria, rather than waiting through staged trials to escalate. Where can I read the full AAP guideline myself? The official Clinical Practice Guideline is published in Pediatrics (Hampl SE et al., 2023, doi:10.1542/peds.2022-060640) and the AAP also publishes a Summary of Key Action Statements PDF. Both are linked in the Sources section below. This page summarizes and explains the guideline in plain language; it is not the official guideline and is not a substitute for reading the primary source. Next steps If you want a pediatric obesity medicine specialist to help you and your teen apply the AAP framework, start a Blueberry Balance visit. Balance works alongside your child's existing pediatrician; our team is led by board-certified pediatricians with DABOM credentialing, and the protocol maps directly to the framework above. title: Crash Champions Empowers Team Members with AI and Tools from CCC
summary: Crash Champions expands use of CCC's AI-powered Mobile Jumpstart 2.0, helping teams work more efficiently while delivering exceptional customer experiences.
body_text: About CCC CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC), a subsidiary of CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: CCC), is a leading SaaS and AI platform provider for the multi-trillion-dollar insurance economy, creating intelligent experiences for insurers, repairers, automakers, part suppliers, and more. The CCC Intelligent Experience (IX) Cloud™ platform, powered by proven AI and an innovative event-based architecture, connects more than 35,000 businesses to power customized applications and platforms for optimal outcomes and personalized experiences that just work. Through purposeful innovation and the strength of its connections, CCC technologies empower the people and industry relied upon to keep lives moving forward when it matters most. Learn more about CCC at www.cccis.com. title: 74% of Gen Z want small town trips over big cities—three creatives lead the way
summary: A new campaign pairs Precious Renee Tucker, Zack Fox and Xaviersobased with three hidden gem American towns, tapping into Gen Z's growing appetite for domestic discovery.
body_text: Gen Z is done waiting for a place to trend before booking it. Nearly half of Gen Z’s trending fall destinations this year are small towns rather than major cities or well-known hotspots, according to internal Airbnb data1. To meet that shift, we’re launching ‘have u considered,’ a campaign that reframes three under-the-radar American towns as must-visit destinations. Pianist Precious Renee Tucker, comedian, multihyphenate Zack Fox, and rapper-producer Xaviersobased are stepping in as destination insiders, each introducing their own audience to a town most people have never thought to visit: Hot Springs, AR; Bemidji, MN; and Gibsonton, FL. A companion survey found that 74 percent of Gen Z travelers are likely to choose a small or lesser-known town over a major city for a leisure trip in the next 12 months, and 63 percent said being early to a place feels like a status symbol2. Affordability remains a driving factor for Gen Z group travel—58 percent say an affordable total price is the most important feature when choosing where to stay; 70 percent still want to prioritize fun travel even when money is tight3. ‘have u considered’ marks the start of a broader shift toward off-the-map American destinations, and with millions of hosts offering stays far beyond the well-worn tourist map, Airbnb is where travelers can find homes in not just these three towns, but countless other hidden gems still waiting to be discovered. Hot Springs, AR, with Precious Renee Tucker Tucker, the Arkansas-born pianist known for playing four keyboards at once, brings a personal connection to Hot Springs—a city built around the thermal springs that made it one of the country’s first federally protected destinations, predating Yellowstone by 40 years. Beyond Bathhouse Row’s historic Victorian-era bathhouses, downtown Hot Springs is a walkable mix of live music venues, lake access, and historic architecture. Guests can experience Hot Springs the way Tucker does, from a walkable cottage to a stay overlooking the lake: Bayou Lake House on Lake Hamilton Fast WiFi, SmartTv, 1 Mile Downtown & Bathhouse MacArthur Geodesic Dome | Starlight Haven 1 / 3 Gibsonton, FL, with Xaviersobased For Xaviersobased, Gibsonton’s legacy as the winter headquarters of the American circus and carnival industry—where performers once kept exotic animals on their own properties and built homes as unusual as their acts—was an easy fit for his own ethos. Just south of Tampa along the Alafia River, the town earned the nickname “Showtown, USA” for the sideshow legends, from giants to bearded ladies, who called it home during the off-season. “’ Gibsonton is for sure based and fits this philosophy because the town is wacky, different and follows its own rules ,” said Xaviersobased. He knows small town travel is having its moment, “the new generation is always down to discover these crazy new places.” Guests can stay along the same river that once anchored Gibsonton’s sideshow community: Modern Waterfront Home • Large Yard • Secluded The Guest House at Riverbend Retreat Fla. Waterfront Studio with Kayak, Dock & Boat Ramp 1 / 3 Bemidji, MN, with Zack Fox Fox sees the hidden-gem travel moment as a reaction to feeling sold to everywhere else. “This generation is hungry to find and make spaces where they’re not being sold something every two seconds,” said Fox. “Once you escape the big cities you see the kids thriving in a new way.” Fox said Airbnb fits how he actually travels. “I travel spontaneously and I consistently need new strange experiences, and Airbnb is the only app that can keep up,” he said. For Fox, the appeal of a town like Bemidji is what’s missing as much as what’s there. “Seeing how real Americans live, and the diversity of layouts outside of urban environments,” he said. “I’m an actor so I like prioritizing time to hang out and absorb real life without the noise of ‘networking’ culture or social media metrics. Americans are hilarious and you gotta go find them.” Asked to make the case for Bemidji over a more Instagram-famous destination, Fox didn’t hold back: “Stop being scared to change your brain chemistry with unfamiliar experiences, it’s unbecoming.” Guests looking to unplug the way Fox describes can find their own version of it in Bemidji: The White House Cozy Lakefront TimberRidge Cabin Biji Blue 1 / 3

title: Slidesgo Alternatives: 9 Better Tools to Try in 2026
summary: Slidesgo alternatives range from free template libraries to full AI deck generators. I reviewed dozens to find the 9 for cleaner presentations in 2026.
body_text: August 5th, 2026 Slidesgo Alternatives: 9 Better Tools to Try in 2026 By Drew Hahn · 23 min read X LinkedIn Slidesgo alternatives fall into three camps: free template libraries that work like Slidesgo, AI tools that generate the whole deck for you, and full design suites you build inside. The strongest picks are Canva for all-around design, Gamma for AI-generated decks, and SlidesCarnival if you just want more free templates. I looked at pricing pages, feature lists, and user reviews across 9 tools to build this list. You'll get the strengths, trade-offs, and best fit for every tool below. 9 best Slidesgo alternatives: TL;DR Canva: Best for marketers who need a polished, on-brand deck without a design background Gamma: Best for anyone who wants to turn a rough outline into a full deck in minutes Beautiful.ai: Best for teams that want every slide to look consistent without manual formatting Julius: Best for turning data directly into a presentation Prezi: Best for presenters who want a moving, story-driven format instead of static slides Pitch: Best for teams building and reviewing decks together in real time Plus AI: Best for people who work in PowerPoint or Google Slides and don't want another app SlidesCarnival: Best for anyone who wants a free Slidesgo-style template library SlidesMania: Best for educators who want free, interactive Google Slides and PowerPoint themes Why look for Slidesgo alternatives? Slidesgo earns its spot as a first stop for a reason. The template library is huge, free to browse, and polished enough to make a rushed deck look like it took time to build. I've grabbed a template from it myself when a meeting got moved up with no warning, and it did the job. The trouble starts once presentations turn into a weekly habit. A few patterns show up fast once you're building decks regularly: Download limits cap your options: The free tier only gives you so many templates a month, and the strongest designs sit behind a Slidesgo Premium or Freepik subscription. Templates need real cleanup: They look great empty, then you're manually fixing spacing, structure, and brand colors once your actual content goes in. There's no editor or AI built in: You get a file, not a workflow. No content generation, no built-in editing, and no way to collaborate with a team. Your decks start to blend in: Pull from the same library long enough and your presentations start looking like everyone else's. 💡 Tip: Explore more AI-first options in our roundup of the best AI presentation makers . Which Slidesgo alternative should you choose? The right pick depends on how much design control you want, whether you're building alone or with a team, and how much AI help you're looking for. Choose: Canva if you want an all-round design suite you can also use for other visual content. Its presentation templates are strong but not built specifically for slide decks, so branding and structure take manual work. Gamma if you want AI to write and build the deck from a prompt. The output usually needs editing before it's ready to present. Beautiful.ai if you build recurring business decks and want them auto-formatted and consistent. That consistency comes from templates, so design freedom is more limited than a full suite. Julius if your deck depends on live data and you want the analysis and the slides to come from the same workflow. It can build from a template and apply your branding automatically, so it's not limited to plain, data-only slides. Prezi if you want non-linear, story-driven presentations. That format takes some getting used to and doesn't suit a standard business deck. Pitch if your team co-builds decks together. Solo users won't get much value from the collaboration features. Plus AI if you want deck generation inside PowerPoint or Google Slides. You're locked into those two ecosystems, since there's no standalone editor. Stick with Slidesgo if you want a free template fast and don't need an editor, AI help, or collaboration, and you're comfortable with the download limits and manual cleanup that come with it. 9 best Slidesgo alternatives: at a glance 💻 Tool 🏷️ Type 🎯 Best for 🔥 Starting price (billed annually) Canva Design suite All-round design and quick branded decks $144/year Gamma AI generator Full decks from a text prompt $9/seat/month Beautiful.ai AI generator Auto-formatted, consistent business decks $12/month Julius AI data analysis and presentation tool Turning data directly into a presentation $16/month Prezi Design suite Non-linear, story-driven presentations $7/month Pitch Design suite Collaborative team decks $13/month Plus AI AI generator Deck generation inside PowerPoint and Google Slides $10/user/month SlidesCarnival Free template library The closest free swap for Slidesgo Free SlidesMania Free template library Free, interactive templates for educators Free *Pricing correct as of July 2026. Verify with vendor. 9 best Slidesgo alternatives 1. Canva: Best for marketers and non-designers who want fast, branded decks Canva is a design suite that lets you create presentations, social graphics, documents, and video in one editor. It gives users a large template library and a drag-and-drop interface that makes branded decks quick to build. PowerPoint exports may need extra cleanup once you pull them out of the platform. Key features Magic Design: Generate a presentation draft from a text prompt or an uploaded image. Brand kit: Store logos, fonts, and colors for use across presentations and other content types. Real-time collaboration: Allow multiple users to edit, comment, and share a deck at the same time. Pros ✅ The template library covers presentations, social graphics, print, and video in one place ✅ The free plan includes presentation creation and basic AI tools ✅ Files export to PowerPoint and Google Slides for use outside Canva Cons ❌ PowerPoint exports aren't always pixel-perfect and can need cleanup ❌ The strongest stock assets and AI features sit behind the paid Pro plan Best for Marketers who need branded decks without a design background Teams that want presentations, social graphics, and video handled in one place Freelancers who want an easy drag-and-drop editor Pricing Canva starts at $144 per year . 2. Gamma: Best for AI-generated decks from a prompt Gamma is an AI presentation tool that generates both content and design from a single prompt . It handles interactive elements such as embedded video, GIFs, and responsive charts, which gives presentations more depth than a static template allows. The AI output still needs a review pass for accuracy and tone before it's ready to present. 💡 Tip: Not sold on Gamma? Check out our guide on the top 10 Gamma alternatives . Key features Prompt-to-deck: Generate slide content and design from a text prompt or an uploaded document. Interactive elements: Embed video, GIFs, and responsive charts within a deck. One-click restyling: Reformat an entire deck's visual style without rebuilding individual slides. Pros ✅ Generates a real content draft, giving you something to edit from the start ✅ Interactive output works well for links, webinars, and sales follow-ups ✅ Free tier is enough to try the core workflow before paying Cons ❌ Free-plan AI credits are a one-time allotment that can run out quickly with regular use ❌ PowerPoint export loses interactive elements and converts them to static images, and it's only available on paid plans Best for Marketers who want a full draft generated from a single prompt Teams that want interactive elements like video and charts built into a deck Users trying out an AI-first workflow before committing to a paid plan Pricing Gamma starts at $9 per seat per month . 3. Beautiful.ai: Best for auto-formatted, consistent business decks Beautiful.ai is a presentation tool built around Smart Slides that adjust spacing, alignment, and layout automatically as you add content. It keeps recurring decks like proposals, pitches, and weekly reports consistent without manual formatting work. Precise, custom placement is harder to achieve, since the system will override manual adjustments. 💡 Tip: Learn more in our in-depth Beautiful.ai review . Key features Smart Slides: Rebalance layouts automatically as slide content changes. AI content generation: Draft slide text and outlines from a prompt. Brand kit and shared libraries: Store visual assets for consistent team decks. Pros ✅ Layouts stay clean across a full deck with almost no manual formatting ✅ PowerPoint exports are predictable and hold their formatting ✅ Well-suited for teams that value consistency over creative freedom Cons ❌ Layout flexibility is limited, and precise placement or custom frameworks are hard to build ❌ Template selection is smaller than Slidesgo's library Best for Sales and marketing teams producing repeatable, on-brand decks Teams that want consistent formatting without manual design work Users who prefer structure over full creative control Pricing Beautiful.ai starts at $12 per month . 4. Julius: Best for turning data directly into a presentation Julius is an AI data analysis tool that turns your questions into charts, insights, and a finished presentation . You can ask a question in plain English, and Julius builds the analysis, then carries it straight into slides. Manual, slide-by-slide design work isn't the strength here, since the workflow starts from a data question and a prompt. Key features Zero-upload data search: Search the web for public datasets or pull financial data through the Financial Datasets partnership without a file to start. Natural language analysis: Ask a question in plain English and get back a chart or a written breakdown. AI presentation maker : Turn a prompt or a finished analysis into a full deck, with hundreds of templates and brand colors and fonts applied automatically. Pros ✅ Users can start from a question instead of needing a file ready to upload ✅ Charts and analysis carry directly into a presentation without a separate design step ✅ Connected data gets faster and more precise to query with each use, since Julius learns the structure and relationships of connected sources over time Cons ❌ Best suited for decks built from a prompt or existing data, rather than heavy manual design work slide by slide ❌ Non-technical users may need a short learning curve to get comfortable phrasing data questions well Best for Finance and operations teams building decks around live data Marketers who want campaign dashboards turned into a shareable presentation Teams that want one workflow instead of switching between an analysis tool and a design tool Pricing Julius starts at $16 per month . 5. Prezi: Best for non-linear, story-driven presentations Prezi replaces the slide-after-slide format with a zoomable canvas that lets you move between ideas by zooming in and out, turning a presentation into a guided story. Sales pitches and teaching sessions benefit most, since the format shows how ideas connect. A poorly built Prezi can make an audience feel a little dizzy, and the canvas takes practice to use well. 💡 Tip: Not sure about Prezi? Check out our guide on the 9 best Prezi alternatives . Key features Zoomable canvas: Build a presentation as a connected map of ideas instead of separate slides. Video overlay: Place yourself on camera alongside your content during remote presentations. AI content generation: Draft slide content and layout from a prompt. Pros ✅ The non-linear canvas creates memorable, story-driven presentations ✅ Video overlay works well for remote and webinar delivery ✅ AI generation and auto-branding have sped up the design process Cons ❌ The canvas format takes real practice for anyone used to traditional slides ❌ Not well suited for formal, data-heavy, or clean PowerPoint handoffs Best for Educators who want to show how ideas connect visually Sales presenters building a memorable, story-driven pitch Remote presenters who want video overlay during a talk Pricing Prezi starts at $7 per month . 6. Pitch: Best for collaborative team decks Pitch is a presentation tool built around teams working on decks together . It combines AI slide generation with real-time co-editing, slide assignments, comments, and engagement analytics that show which slides recipients spend time on. PowerPoint export isn't available until the Team plan, and even then it can need cleanup for animations and embedded elements. Key features Real-time co-editing: Assign slides, add comments, and edit a deck together at the same time. Engagement analytics: Track which slides recipients open and spend time on. AI slide generation: Draft slide content and layout from a prompt. Pros ✅ Real-time collaboration includes slide assignments and comments ✅ Engagement analytics show how recipients interact with shared decks ✅ Free plan includes unlimited presentations Cons ❌ Design customization is limited for precise or complex layouts ❌ PowerPoint export can need cleanup for animations and embedded elements Best for Sales teams that co-build and share decks regularly Startups that want engagement data on shared presentations Teams that need slide assignments and comments in one workflow Pricing Pitch starts at $13 per month . 7. Plus AI: Best for deck generation inside PowerPoint and Google Slides Plus AI works as an add-on inside Google Slides and PowerPoint , generating full presentations from a prompt or an uploaded document. Teams keep their files in Google Drive or OneDrive, so nobody has to learn a new editor. The PowerPoint version trails Google Slides in polish, and technical content sometimes needs a design pass afterward. Key features Prompt-to-deck: Generate a structured slide deck from a text prompt, a PDF, or a Word document. Remix: Convert existing slides into a new layout or format with one click. Brand themes: Store logos, colors, and custom instructions for consistent team output on higher plans. Pros ✅ Presentations build and edit directly inside Google Slides or PowerPoint ✅ Hundreds of layouts give the AI output more design variety than most add-ons ✅ Collaboration and file storage stay tied to Google Drive or OneDrive What users say ❌ The PowerPoint add-on experience lags behind the Google Slides version ❌ There's no free plan, so trying the tool requires payment upfront Best for Teams that want AI generation without leaving PowerPoint or Google Slides Users who prefer editing inside a familiar tool over a separate platform Teams already working in Google Drive or Microsoft 365 that want AI added on Pricing Plus AI starts at $10 per user per month . Special mentions These two tools cover the same ground as Slidesgo itself: free templates without an editor or AI layer. Here are 2 more worth a look if that's exactly what you need: SlidesCarnival : A free template library for Google Slides and PowerPoint, with a design style close enough to Slidesgo that switching over feels familiar. There's no editor or AI features, so you're still building the deck yourself after downloading a template. SlidesMania : A free library of Google Slides and PowerPoint themes with a strong focus on interactive elements like clickable buttons and embedded video. Educators use it often for lesson templates, though the library covers general presentations too. Downloads work the same way as Slidesgo, a template first, and you build the rest. How to evaluate Slidesgo alternatives My advice after going through all 9 tools: check how each one handles PowerPoint export during evaluation. Interactive elements like embedded video or animations don't always survive the trip out of the platform, and that's a detail worth catching early, before you've built a workflow around a tool your client can't open the way you expect. Consider: How much design control you want: Some tools hand you a template and step out of the way. Others, like Beautiful.ai, auto-format the layout for you and push back if you try to move things too far off-script. I'd think about which one annoys you the least before committing. Whether AI-generated content needs a review pass: Tools like Gamma can draft a full deck from a prompt, but the copy usually needs editing for accuracy and tone. If you're on a tight deadline, budget time for that pass and don’t assume the first draft is presentation-ready. How your team works together: A handful of these tools build in comments, slide assignments, and shared brand kits, and a handful don't. If you're the only one touching the deck, that feature barely matters. If 3 people are editing it before a client call, it matters a lot. Whether you need a clean PowerPoint file at the end: Some tools export cleanly, and others hand you a link or a PDF that loses interactivity the moment it leaves the platform. I'd check this before you build a habit around a tool your client can't open. Turn your data into a finished deck Design is one part of building a deck. If your presentation depends on numbers, most Slidesgo alternatives still leave you with a blank template and the data work still ahead of you. Julius starts from the data instead . You can search the web for public datasets, pull company financials through the Financial Datasets partnership, or connect your own sources, then ask questions in plain English. The AI presentation maker turns that analysis into a full deck using templates, ready to export as PPT, PDF, or Google Slides. Start your free Julius trial today . Frequently asked questions What is the best free Slidesgo alternative? SlidesMania is the best fully free alternative , with creative, interactive templates and no download limits or premium tier. SlidesCarnival works well as a like-for-like swap for general use, and Canva's free plan adds a broader design toolkit if you need one. Is Slidesgo actually free? No, Slidesgo isn't fully free . The free tier includes thousands of templates, but it caps monthly downloads and keeps its best designs behind a Slidesgo Premium or Freepik subscription. SlidesMania and Canva's free plan offer more generous unlimited access. Can AI presentation tools really replace templates? Yes, AI tools like Gamma can replace a template for a first draft , since they generate a full deck from a prompt faster than browsing a library. The output still needs a review pass for accuracy and tone before it's ready to present. Which Slidesgo alternative is best for business presentations? Beautiful.ai suits teams producing consistent recurring decks, Canva covers all-round business design, and Julius fits data-heavy reports where the numbers need to hold up. All three offer stronger brand control and collaboration than Slidesgo. Which Slidesgo alternative is best for teachers? SlidesMania is the top choice for teachers , with free gamified templates, interactive quizzes, and digital notebooks built for classroom engagement. Canva for Education is another option if your school provides access.

title: Gabriel Martins’ ‘On Behalf of My Son’ Selected for San Sebastián Film Festival Competition
summary: On Behalf of My Son, the new film by Minas Gerais-born director Gabriel Martins, has been selected for the 74th San Sebastian International Film Festival in Spain, in the Official Selection (Sección Oficial).
body_text: São Paulo, August 14, 2026 - On Behalf of My Son , the new film by Minas Gerais-born director Gabriel Martins, has been selected for the 74th San Sebastian International Film Festival in Spain, in the Official Selection (Sección Oficial) - the festival’s competitive section featuring its main titles in competition. The film is running for the Golden Shell, the festival’s top prize, which will take place from September 18 to 26. “I feel very honored to be part of such a prestigious and long-standing festival for the first time, especially as part of the official competition. I feel this will be another important step in the film’s journey, elevating the work not only of our cast and crew, but also of Brazilian cinema,” says Gabriel Martins, the film’s director. The result of a partnership between Netflix and production company Filmes de Plástico, On Behalf of My Son tell the story of a mother who decides to seek out the families of the victims of a tragedy involving her son. In the film, Vicentina (Rejane Faria) must deal with the aftermath of her son Wesley’s death in a bus accident in which he was the driver. As the investigation unfolds, evidence suggests that Wesley’s action may have been intentional. Vicentina then embarks on a courageous journey to find the victims’ families and apologize, while being forced to confront her own grief and deepest uncertainties. The film’s selection in San Sebastián also marks another special moment for Brazilian cinema and, above all, for the director’s home state. Set in Minas Gerais, where Gabriel Martins was born and raised, the film adds to a standout year for the state’s film industry on the international festival circuit. “I also celebrate this selection as another achievement for cinema from Minas Gerais, which has been having a remarkable year in 2026, starting with the Berlin Film Festival. This makes me very happy for the local artists and excited about the next steps for this generation that I am part of.” Directed and written by Gabriel Martins, from an original story by the filmmaker, On Behalf of My Son stars Rejane Faria in the lead role and features some of the most prominent names in Brazilian cinema, including Maíra Azevedo, Flavio Bauraqui, Giovanna Heliodoro, Giovanni Venturini, Grace Passô, Karine Teles, Renato Novaes, and Thalma de Freitas. On Behalf of My Son premieres in 2026. About On Behalf of My Son Synopsis: On a sunny morning in the city of Belo Horizonte, a crowded public bus makes its way downtown. As it crosses an overpass, the vehicle suddenly swerves, veers off the road, and crashes onto the avenue below. One passenger is left critically injured, while everyone else -- including Wesley, the driver -- is killed. The tragedy dominates television broadcasts and newspaper headlines across the country. Security cameras from both the bus and the roadway capture the moment of the crash, and after the footage is analyzed, speculation begins to spread that the driver may have acted intentionally. Vicentina, a 75-year-old retired schoolteacher and Wesley’s mother, is devastated by the tragedy and uncertain of how to move forward. She decides to seek out the victims’ families and apologize. The road ahead proves difficult to navigate, and the answers Vicentina longs for are not always the ones she finds. Director: Gabriel Martins Producer: Thiago Macêdo Correia Original Story: Gabriel Martins Screenplay: Gabriel Martins Music: Tiganá Santana Cinematography: Leonardo Feliciano Editing: Gabriel Martins, Thiago Ricarte Sound: Tiago Bello (Edição e Mixagem); Gustavo Fioravante (Gravação) Production Design: Rimenna Procópio Costume Design: Diana Moreira Special Effects: Rodrigo Jinks, Marcelo Cabral, Cajamanga, Quanta Production Company: Filmes de Plástico Cast: Rejane Faria (Vicentina); Maíra Azevedo (Joana); Renato Novaes (Wesley/Bruno); Giovanni Venturini (Fred); Giovanna Heliodoro (Gisele); Grace Passô (Isabel); Marisa Revert (Vera); Fernanda Vianna (Marta); Clébia Sousa (Solange); Fábio Leal (Victor); Docy Moreira (Marluce); Carlos Francisco (Antônio); Thalma de Freitas (Cleide); Flavio Bauraqui (Luiz); Bárbara Colen (Amélia); presenting Miguelzinho do Cavaco (Himself). About Netflix: Netflix is one of the world’s leading entertainment services offering TV series, films, games and live programming across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time. About Filmes de Plástico Founded in 2009 by André Novais Oliveira, Gabriel Martins, Maurilio Martins, and Thiago Macêdo Correia, FILMES DE PLÁSTICO is one of Brazil's leading film production companies, recognized for films that portray Black and working-class communities with honesty and dignity. Its productions have been screened and awarded at major international festivals — such as Cannes, Berlin, Sundance, Locarno, and Rotterdam — and, in 2023, the company represented Brazil as the official submission for the 95th Academy Awards® with the film Mars One ( Marte Um ). In addition to developing its own projects locally, the production company also works to train and foster new talent within its community. Press Contacts Ágora Agency | netflix@agora.site
